top_temples.name: Narmada Udgam Temple (Narmadakund)
top_temples.location_note: Marks the source of the Narmada river; the central shrine of Amarkantak, surrounded by a cluster of smaller temples including Shiva, Karthikeya, and Annapurna shrines.

top_temples.name: Kapil Dhara Temple
top_temples.deity: Shiva, associated with sage Kapil Muni
top_temples.location_note: Near the Kapildhara waterfall on the Narmada, a short distance from the main Narmadakund complex in Amarkantak.

top_temples.name: Birla Mandir (Lakshmi Narayan Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Atop Shyamla Hills, Bhopal; overlooks the Upper Lake, a major city landmark.

top_temples.name: Bhojeshwar Temple (Bhojpur Temple)
top_temples.location_note: About 32 km from Bhopal on Hoshangabad Road; an unfinished 11th-century temple housing one of the world's largest monolithic Shivalingas.

top_temples.name: Gufa Mandir (Cave Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Bhopal; a Shiva shrine established within a rock cave.

top_temples.name: Manuabhan Tekri Jain Temple
top_temples.location_note: Atop Manuabhan hill in Bhopal; a small but notable Jain shrine.

top_temples.name: Sri Radha Krishna Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Bhopal; open to devotees throughout the day.

top_temples.name: Kamadgiri Temple
top_temples.location_note: Considered the heart of Chitrakoot, on a forested hill straddling the Madhya Pradesh-Uttar Pradesh border; the town's defining pilgrimage site.

top_temples.name: Bharat Milap Temple
top_temples.location_note: Along the Kamadgiri Parikrama path in Chitrakoot; marks the spot where Bharata is believed to have met Rama during his exile.

top_temples.name: Maa Chamunda Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Atop the Chamunda hill (Devi Tekri) in Dewas city; one of the two defining hilltop Devi shrines of Dewas.

top_temples.name: Jay Maa Tulja Bhavani (Badi Mata) Mandir
top_temples.location_note: On the adjacent Devi Tekri hill in Dewas, alongside the Chamunda shrine; a major Shakti temple of the Malwa region.

top_temples.name: Kaila Devi Mandir
top_temples.location_note: In the heart of Dewas city; one of its oldest temples.

top_temples.name: Mata Tekri Shankh Duvar
top_temples.location_note: A notable Devi shrine near Dewas.

top_temples.name: Dasha Mata Mandir
top_temples.location_note: A local Devi shrine within Dewas city.

top_temples.name: Sahastrabahu Temple (Saas-Bahu Ka Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: 11th-century twin sandstone temple within Gwalior Fort, renowned for its architecture.

top_temples.name: Sun Temple (Surya Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: Gwalior; noted for its sculptural depiction of the sun god.

top_temples.name: Teli Ka Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Within Gwalior Fort; built around the 9th century, the tallest structure in the fort, blending Dravidian and North Indian styles.

top_temples.name: Shri Koteshwar Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: Gwalior; walls and ceilings depict scenes from Shiva mythology.

top_temples.name: Chaturbhuj Temple
top_temples.location_note: Near Man Mandir Palace within Gwalior Fort complex.

top_temples.name: Khajrana Ganesh Temple
top_temples.location_note: Built by Rani Ahilyabai Holkar in Indore; one of the city's most visited shrines, known for its mythological engravings.

top_temples.name: Bijasan Mata Temple
top_temples.location_note: Indore; heavily visited during Navaratri.

top_temples.name: Annapurna Temple
top_temples.location_note: Among Indore's most prominent temples.

top_temples.name: Ranjeet Hanuman Temple
top_temples.location_note: Also known as Pritra Parvat; a well-known Hanuman shrine in Indore.

top_temples.name: Kanch Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Bijasan Mata Road, Indore; a Jain temple built around 1903 with an interior crafted entirely from glass and mirrors.

top_temples.name: Chausath Yogini Temple
top_temples.location_note: Built in the 10th century by the Kalachuri dynasty in Jabalpur; features 64 carved Yogini statues in a style resembling Khajuraho.

top_temples.name: Tripur Sundari Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Tewar village, about 12 km from Jabalpur on the Bhedaghat road; a place of worship since the 11th century Kalachuri era.

top_temples.name: Sri Gupteshwar Mahadev Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Jabalpur; a swayambhu (self-manifested) Siddha Peetha.

top_temples.name: Pisanhari Ki Madiya
top_temples.location_note: A roughly 500-year-old Digambar Jain hilltop temple complex in Jabalpur.

top_temples.name: Paat Baba Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Jabalpur; founded in 1903 by a British officer near the Gun Carriage Factory.

top_temples.name: Kandariya Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: The largest of the Western Group of Temples in Khajuraho; over 31 m tall with more than 870 sculptures, UNESCO World Heritage Site.

top_temples.name: Chausath Yogini Temple, Khajuraho
top_temples.location_note: Western Group, Khajuraho; the only granite-built temple in the complex, dating to the 9th century, considered the oldest surviving structure there.

top_temples.name: Maa Sharda Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Atop Trikoota Hill in Maihar, reached via 1,063 steps; one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, dated to around 502 AD.

top_temples.name: Chaturbhuj Temple, Maihar Fort
top_temples.location_note: Within the Maihar Fort complex, alongside subsidiary shrines to Bala Ganapathi, Muruga, and Adi Shankara; a distinct shrine from the main Sharda Devi temple.

top_temples.name: Shri Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga Temple
top_temples.location_note: On an island (Mandhata) in the Narmada river; one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, a five-storied temple with different deities on each floor.

top_temples.name: Mamleshwar (Amareshwar) Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the southern bank of the Narmada, opposite Omkareshwar; a separate ancient temple with inscriptions dating to 1063 AD, visited alongside Omkareshwar.

top_temples.name: Ram Raja Temple
top_temples.location_note: Built in the 16th century by Queen Ganesh Kunwari; the only temple where Rama is worshipped as a ruling king, complete with a ceremonial guard salute.

top_temples.name: Chaturbhuj Temple
top_temples.location_note: Orchha; 16th-century Bundela-built temple originally intended to house the Ram Raja idol before it stayed at its present site.

top_temples.name: Jata Shankar Cave Temple
top_temples.location_note: A limestone cave shrine about 1.5 km from Pachmarhi bus station; stalagmite formations are revered as 108 natural lingams.

top_temples.name: Chauragarh Temple (Chhota Mahadeo)
top_temples.location_note: Atop Chauragarh Hill (1,330 m), Pachmarhi's third-highest peak; built during the 14th-century Gond dynasty, known for thousands of trishuls left by devotees.

top_temples.name: Kalika Mata Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Hilltop temple overlooking Ratlam city; believed over 300 years old, the city's most prominent temple, major Navratri fair.

top_temples.name: Mahalakshmi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Central Ratlam; especially visited during Diwali.

top_temples.name: Kedareshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Heart of Ratlam city; known for ancient architecture and carvings.

top_temples.name: Bilpakeshwara Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the Mhow-Neemuch Highway in Ratlam city.

top_temples.name: Sagod Jain Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the national highway in Ratlam city.

top_temples.name: Shiv Temple (Baina Ganga / 12 Jyotirlinga Shrine)
top_temples.location_note: Sagar; a large Shiva temple where representations of all 12 Jyotirlingas can be viewed, major Mahashivratri celebration.

top_temples.name: Shri Dev Ram Bagh Mandir
top_temples.location_note: On Sarafa Bazar's main street in Sagar; one of the city's oldest temples.

top_temples.name: Moraji Digambar Jain Temple
top_temples.location_note: Sagar city; also runs an associated Sanskrit school.

top_temples.name: Gopal Ji Temple
top_temples.location_note: A notable temple within Sagar city.

top_temples.name: Jwala Mata Mandir
top_temples.location_note: A local Devi shrine in Sagar.

top_temples.name: Venkatesh Temple
top_temples.location_note: Mukhtyarganj, Satna; built in 1876 of red stone beside a reflecting pond.

top_temples.name: Pashupati Nath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Satna city; a well-known Shiva shrine.

top_temples.name: Vaishno Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Satna city; a local Devi pilgrimage shrine.

top_temples.name: Belatgiri Temple
top_temples.location_note: On a rocky hill in Satna district.

top_temples.name: Golamath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Satna; built during the Kalachuri period (10th-11th century AD), believed to fulfill devotees' prayers.

top_temples.name: Mahakaleshwar Temple, Seoni
top_temples.location_note: Seoni; a locally prominent Shiva shrine popular with tourists and devotees, distinct from the Ujjain Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga.

top_temples.name: Chhindimatta Temple
top_temples.location_note: Hilltop shrine near Seoni with panoramic views.

top_temples.name: Dighori Temple (Adi Shankaracharya Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Dighori village, Seoni district; believed built by the philosopher Adi Shankaracharya.

top_temples.name: Matradham Mandir
top_temples.location_note: A popular pilgrimage location in Seoni.

top_temples.name: Jagdish Mandir
top_temples.location_note: One of Seoni's well-known city temples.

top_temples.name: Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga Temple
top_temples.location_note: Ujjain's defining shrine; one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, site of the daily Bhasma Aarti.

top_temples.name: Kal Bhairav Temple
top_temples.location_note: Ujjain; the most important of the eight Bhairava shrines, known for its unique liquor offering tradition.

top_temples.name: Mangalnath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Ujjain; the only temple in India dedicated to the planet Mars, believed to be its birthplace in Hindu astrology.

top_temples.name: Navagraha Temple
top_temples.location_note: On Triveni Ghat, banks of the Shipra river, Ujjain; said to be India's first Navagraha temple, over 2,000 years old.

top_temples.name: Gadkalika Temple
top_temples.location_note: Ujjain; associated with the poet Kalidasa, who is said to have worshipped here and gained his poetic gifts.
